ic_name: TIA/EIA-485 (RS-485 via TI SLLA272C Design Guide)

protocol_overview.type: Balanced differential multipoint serial transmission line (electrical-only standard).
protocol_overview.duplex: Half-duplex on a 2-wire (1 differential-pair) bus; full-duplex on a 4-wire (2 differential-pairs) bus.
protocol_overview.physical_signaling: Differential pair — non-inverting line A and inverting line B; differential voltage Vab = Va - Vb encodes the bit. |Vab| > +200 mV at receiver = mark; Vab < -200 mV = space.
protocol_overview.bus_topology: Daisy-chain / party-line / linear bus. Drivers, receivers and transceivers connect to a single main cable trunk via short network stubs.
protocol_overview.addressing: RS-485 itself has no addressing; higher-level protocols (Modbus RTU, DL/T645, BACnet MS/TP, …) carry addresses on top of the byte stream.
protocol_overview.bus_value_idle_recommendation: Determined by external or internal fail-safe biasing — typically pulls A high and B low so |Vab| > 200 mV in the marking direction when no driver is active.

functional_requirements.text: All signaling between bus nodes is differential between non-inverting line A and inverting line B.
RS-485-compliant driver produces a minimum 1.5 V differential output across a 54-ohm test load (= two 120-ohm terminations in parallel + 32 unit loads).
RS-485-compliant receiver detects a differential input as low as ±200 mV across the full common-mode range.
Bus common-mode voltage range is -7 V to +12 V referenced to receiver ground; receiver must operate over this entire range.
Standard-compliant driver must be able to drive 32 unit loads (UL); a unit load = ~12 kohm impedance per Section 8 of SLLA272D.
1/8-UL transceivers allow up to 32 / (1/8) = 256 nodes; failsafe biasing consumes up to 20 UL, reducing the practical maximum to (32 - 20) / 0.125 = 96 with 1/8-UL parts.
Cable trunk must be terminated at each end with a resistor matching the characteristic impedance (typically 120 ohm for industrial UTP cable).
Maximum stub length L_stub ≤ (tr / 10) × v × c where tr = driver 10/90 rise time, v = cable signal velocity factor, c = speed of light. Drivers with longer rise times tolerate longer stubs.

Maximum cable length is limited by transmission-line losses and signal jitter; data reliability sharply decreases beyond ~10 % jitter of the baud period. 4000 ft (1200 m) at 100 kbps is the documented standard upper bound. Conservative rule of thumb: line_length [m] × data_rate [bps] < 10^7.

Fail-safe operation = receiver assumes a determined output state during loss-of-signal (open-circuit, short-circuit, or idle-bus). Modern transceivers integrate internal biasing; external resistive divider provides higher noise margin in noisy environments.

Half-duplex direction control: each transceiver has a DE (driver enable, active HIGH) and RE# (receiver enable, active LOW) input. Only one driver may be enabled at any time; software is responsible for ensuring this.
Full-duplex (4-wire) topology uses two differential pairs — one for master-to-slaves transmission, one for slaves-to-master — allowing simultaneous TX and RX without DE/RE# arbitration.
Maximum data rate documented in the standard is 10 Mbps at 40 ft; modern transceivers reach 40 Mbps at short stubs.
Robust links over long distances or large ground-potential differences (GPD) require galvanic isolation of signal AND supply via digital isolators + isolated DC/DC converter at the transceiver.
Minimum node spacing on the bus d > C_L / (5.25 × C') where C_L = lumped load capacitance per node and C' = media capacitance per unit length; chosen to keep loaded bus impedance Z' > 0.4 × Z0.

error_response_conditions: Loss of signal (open-circuit) — bus disconnected; failsafe biasing must drive receiver output to a determined state.
Loss of signal (short-circuit) — insulation fault shorts A to B or to another wire; failsafe biasing or driver short-circuit current limit handles this.
Loss of signal (idle-bus) — all drivers disabled; receiver sees ~0 V Vab; failsafe biasing required.
Bus contention — two drivers enabled simultaneously in half-duplex; must be prevented by software direction control.
Stub-reflection / impedance-mismatch signal-integrity errors — stubs longer than tr × v × c / 10 cause reflections that distort the eye.
Common-mode noise — large ground-potential differences exceed the -7 V to +12 V receiver common-mode range, causing data errors. Mitigation: galvanic isolation.
compliance_requirements: Driver minimum differential output ≥ 1.5 V into 54 ohm load.
Receiver minimum differential input sensitivity ±200 mV.
Receiver common-mode range -7 V to +12 V.
Supports at least 32 unit loads (or scaled equivalent with 1/8-UL parts).
Cable characteristic impedance ≥ 100 ohm; industrial UTP typically 120 ohm.
Termination resistor at each cable end matching cable Z0.
Stub length ≤ tr × v × c / 10 to preserve signal integrity.
Higher-level standards built ON TOP of RS-485 (Modbus RTU, DL/T645, …) provide framing / CRC / addressing — RS-485 itself does not.
external_signal_wire_count: 2 (lines A, B) in half-duplex; 4 (TX-A, TX-B, RX-A, RX-B) in full-duplex. Plus driver-side DE / RE# direction-control digital pins per transceiver.
